timed_text.text: A 23, commitment is about directing your behavior toward your values, not when you feel
like it every day.
One of the most powerful ways to stay anchored to your values is to make them visible.
To build a picture of the life and the athlete you're committed to becoming, and put it
somewhere you see every single day.
Research on visual goal representation shows that when the brain is repeatedly exposed
to images of a desired outcome, it begins to prioritize the information and opportunities
that align with it.
Your attention starts to organize around what you see consistently.
What you see consistently, you move toward.
But this only works if it's real, not generic inspiration, specific images and words that
represent your athletic goals, your identity, the life your committed to build.
There's Canva, images on the internet, words, whatever it takes, but build something
that when you look at it, you feel the pull of it.
The version of yourself on the other side of the work.
On your screen, you'll find the visualization board tool.
Take your time.

blocks.prompt: Build a picture of the athlete you're committing to becoming. Your goals. Your why. Your future. Make it specific enough that looking at it every day means something.

timed_text.text: That board lives on your home screen now.
Look at it every morning before you train,
look at it the night before competition,
look at it when the work gets hard
and the results aren't showing up yet.
That's not decoration, that's a commitment device.
After you finish, day 23 is complete.
